Dear Mr. Scanlon,
Account Reference: DPE-4821
Affected Service Window: September 22 – October 4
Claim Reference: CR-00673

We are writing to express our sincere regret for the delays that affected your shipments during the period indicated above. Of the parcels dispatched under your account, seven experienced delivery times well beyond our standard commitment, and we recognize the inconvenience this has caused your operations.
The disruption resulted from water damage sustained at our Ravenscroft sorting hub, which remains temporarily closed for structural repairs. Sylvia Drummond, who was brought onto our central operations team from the Pembury branch earlier this year, is personally overseeing the restoration effort. Our logistics department has implemented a revised routing plan to prevent further delays.
Your shipments are now being processed through our Wycliffe distribution center. Not until the Ravenscroft hub has been certified for full operations will this interim arrangement be lifted. A written confirmation of your credit will be sent once your claim has been reviewed.
To claim a service credit of $8.50 per affected parcel, please submit your original shipping receipts together with the claim reference noted above.
Sincerely,
Angela Baxter
Senior Coordinator, Customer Care Office
All claims must be received by November 1.

Member Consultation: Proposed Extended Operating Hours
Posted: March 5
Ref: EMP-2024-017
Over the past year, evening and weekend sessions at the pool have experienced a substantial rise in attendance, and usage of the adjacent warm-water area has similarly increased. Several peak-period sessions now regularly reach capacity before all registered members can be accommodated. The facility is therefore proposing three alternative operating-hour patterns and is inviting members to indicate a preference before any change is adopted. --[1]--.
The three proposed options are summarized below.
Option

Weekend Change

Maitland Corporation
Professional Development Fund
Information for All Full-Time Employees
About the Fund
Beginning this quarter, the Professional Development Fund has been expanded to include all full-time employees who have completed at least one year of continuous service with Maitland Corporation. The fund was previously limited to staff in supervisory positions. It now provides partial reimbursement for fees paid toward approved courses offered by outside organizations. Courses in each category are reimbursed at different rates and are subject to different annual ceilings. The complete rate schedule appears below.
How to Apply
The fund was established to
promote
ongoing professional growth throughout the organization. Before enrolling in any outside course, employees must submit a Fund Request Form to the Employee Development Office and receive written confirmation of approval. Applications are typically reviewed within five business days. Courses taken without prior authorization are not eligible for reimbursement under any circumstances. Once an approved course has been completed, the employee should file a reimbursement claim along with the original fee receipt and a certificate of completion or passing grade. Claims must be submitted within 60 days of course completion.
Rate Schedule

Reimbursement Rate
Annual Ceiling
Job-Related Certification
80%
$3,000
General Professional Skills
60%
$1,500

40%

Note: The annual ceiling for each category applies to the combined total of all courses claimed in that category within a single calendar year. Any amount exceeding the ceiling is the responsibility of the employee. Approved reimbursements are paid through the employee's regular paycheck within 30 business days of claim submission.
For the Fund Request Form or any questions about the program, contact the Employee Development Office at Ext. 4720.

Penrose Paint and Color — Customer Feedback
★★★★☆ | Custom Color Matching
Tamara Vogt | Foxwood | September
I brought in a fabric swatch from my living room curtains and asked the counter to match it as a flat wall paint. The staff member who helped me was careful and thorough. He tested several formulas before settling on the right one, and I could tell this is a store that has been doing custom work for quite some time. The shade, which they labeled Warm Linen, was exactly what I wanted. I especially appreciated that they mixed a small trial pot at no extra charge so I could test the color at home before committing to the full order. I placed an order for four cans — two for the living room and two for the bedroom.
When I returned three days later to collect my order, only two cans were ready. The tinting base needed for my shade had run out, so the two bedroom cans could not be mixed. I was disappointed, as I had arranged for a painter to start that weekend. No one had called me in advance.
I plan to order the same shade for my hallway once this is resolved. I hope the store will reach out soon.
3 people found this helpful | Leave a reply

Business Briefs
The Bexley District Business Council has opened applications for its annual Community Improvement Grants. The program provides funding to local organizations for neighborhood projects within the district.
The grants are financed through a portion of annual membership fees paid by the Council's 150 member businesses. Eligible applicants must be registered nonprofit groups and must demonstrate that at least 30 percent of total project value will come from volunteer labor or donated materials. Awards fall into three categories: Public Space Enhancement (up to $4,000), Youth and Education Programs (up to $3,500), and Community Safety Improvements (up to $5,000).
"The strongest proposals bring residents together around a shared goal," said Philip Renwick, chair of the grants committee.
Applications are available at bexleycouncil.example and must be submitted by March 15. Decisions will be announced by April 30.
